thread:
maya: Heads-up — multiple support tickets reporting p95 API latency regressions for APAC customers since ~03:00 UTC. Saw a few traces with an unexpected cross-region hop (apac -> us-east -> apac). customer: CUST-12345. Anyone seeing similar?

sam: Yep seeing it on synthetic probes. p95 for generate-text jumped from 110ms -> 480ms around 03:02. Traceroutes show an extra AS hop, DNS answers look fine but TTLs shifted.

jordan: I pulled a few traces from the edge logs. TLS handshake time spiked for ~10% of flows, connection path contains a IX peering we normally don't use for that prefix. Possible routing flap or bgp change upstream.

lee-oncall: oncall-bot triggered automated alert: `edge-egress-p95-apac > threshold` at 03:05 UTC. Auto-scaling and failover not triggered since throughput normal. Escalating to eng-sre.

amps: (oops) meant to say @sam: can you paste a sample traceroute / mtr?

sam: Sure — sample from apac probe to host api.redwood.ai:```traceroute to api.redwood.ai (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 1.2 ms 1.0 ms 1.1 ms
 2 198.51.100.2 (198.51.100.2) 5.4 ms 5.3 ms 5.2 ms
 3 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45) 480.7 ms 482.1 ms 479.9 ms``` Notice hop2 is our expected edge, hop3 latency jumps — suggests remote route then returns.

jordan: That pattern often means hairpinning — packet leaves APAC to a transit, then back to APAC. Could be an upstream route withdraw and reannouncement.

maya: Quick mitigation idea — can we force route affinity to local-pop for affected prefixes? Maybe apply temporary shorter local BGP community or prefer anycast any-local policy.

infra-bot: Ran `route-probe` against prefix 203.0.113.0/24: returned path set includes transit-AS-9001 -> us-east-AS-701. No recent config changes on our side in the last 24h.

sam: I can push a traffic-shift rule to prefer local pair for that prefix for the next 30m and watch p95. Will do if eng agrees.

jordan: +1. Also suggest bumping TCP handshake retries timeout for probes to reduce measurement noise and enable quick TLS session reuse by increasing session cache window on the APAC edge.

lee-oncall: Go ahead, sam. Notify customers in CUST-12345 ticket and add a note to status page with "investigating". I'll coordinate with support.

sam: Pushed traffic-shift to prefer local POP for 203.0.113.0/24 at 03:15. Watching metrics.

(2m later) sam: p95 dropped to ~120ms for affected probes. Traces show direct APAC POP path restored.

maya: Nice. Jordan — can you follow up with our transit team to request a routemap/AS path cleanup with provider (AS-9001)? We need them to avoid reannouncing via us-east.

jordan: Filing ticket to provider with attached traces and traceroute output. Ticket 9876. Also enabling more aggressive route monitoring for that origin.

lee-oncall: Support update sent to CUST-12345: "We've applied a temporary routing preference to restore local POP egress. We're working with upstream transit to make this stable. Expecting normal latency within minutes. We'll follow up when upstream confirms." :thumbsup:

maya: Follow-up action items: 1) Provider ticket (jordan) 2) Add automated detection rule for cross-region hairpin with p95 delta > 200ms (sam) 3) Postmortem if provider can't justify flapping (owner: maya).

oncall-bot: Auto-acknowledged. Assigned owners recorded.

jordan: Provider responded — they saw a transient BGP flap tied to maintenance at 02:58 UTC, should be resolved. Asked them to prep a stable path and add no-export community for our prefixes.

maya: OK closing thread once provider confirms and metrics stay stable for 2 hours. Thanks all.
